title: Change it, months later
about: Every line of code in this film is read from examples/plugged-in, and every line of terminal output is replayed from docs/manual/captures, recorded by running the commands for real.

pictures.carries: The row of seven operations, one dot each: all green after the full proof, all amber when the rule goes, and still not green at the end. It returns on every sheet.
pictures.rule: You and the designer. An editor on blueprint/things/handle/invariants.ts with the six lines of oneNamePerPerson struck out, replaying captures/change-diff.txt; above it the seven dots, green, from captures/change-impact-before.txt.
pictures.stale: Your agent. A terminal replays captures/change-impact.txt line by line, and as the stale line prints the seven dots turn amber together and the proven count drops to none.
pictures.check: Your agent. A terminal replays captures/change-check.txt with its three parts held open: types, drift and changes; an editor beside it shows the line of src/link/add.ts that read through the rule; then captures/change-generate.txt prints its nine files and the drift part clears.
pictures.red: Your agent, then the author's page. A terminal replays captures/change-prove-changed.txt (all seven chosen, then the build failing), a card marked staged for the stand-in, then captures/change-prove.txt at the journey claim a handle, six of eight, beside the step from journeys/claim-a-handle.ts that says the old rule.
pictures.who: The cast in a row with Kit.who: you, the designer, the author, the builder, each over the one thing they change. A terminal replays captures/change-impact-after.txt and captures/change-version.txt, and Kit.stand marks what ran, what is practice, what was staged and what is missing.

lines.text: Plugged In has been live for months. And you've decided: a person may hold more than one name.
It's one rule. But what was leaning on it?
First, your agent runs the whole proof on the app as it stands. Seven operations, all proven. That's the record the change is measured from.
Then the designer takes the rule out of the blueprint. Six lines, and nothing else. This is the part you read.
Before anything is rebuilt, ask what the change did. The command is ortho impact.
It names the change: the handle's rules, and one operation, handle.claim.
lines.say: It names the change: the handle's rules, and one operation, handle dot claim.

lines.text: Then the cost. Stale: all seven operations. Proven: none.
In an app this small, one rule on the handle unproved everything.
Now the check. It fails, in three parts.
Drift: nine generated files still describe the old rule. That's the framework's own work, and generate rewrites them.
Changes: a refusal your callers could be given is gone. That's counted as a major change.
And types. The handler for link.add no longer fits. It found your page through this rule: one name meant one page.
lines.say: And types. The handler for link dot add no longer fits. It found your page through this rule: one name meant one page.

lines.text: So with two names, which page gets the link? That isn't a builder's question. It comes back to you.

scenes.title: The journey that said the old rule

lines.text: Prove what changed. It can't place the regenerated files, so it chooses all seven journeys. And then it can't run: the app doesn't build.
To see further, we stood in for the builder. The link goes on the oldest name. Nobody decided that.
Now the whole proof. Six journeys pass. Claim a handle: six of eight.
Read the reason. Expected refused, with handle already owned. It answered.
That's the proof working. Months ago, an author wrote the old rule down as a step. The step is still there.
So the red step is the author's to change, and nobody else's. The author also writes the new story: a person with two names adds a link. It fails first.
Only then does a builder take the brief for link.add, and climb.
lines.say: Only then does a builder take the brief for link dot add, and climb.

lines.text: What goes wrong. After a failed proof, impact forgets the change, and calls every operation unproven. So ask before you prove again.
And the next version needs a logbook. On a laptop, we had none.
One honest note. We made the edit ourselves, and the stand-in handler was staged. No author and no builder were filmed, so this film stops at red.
The roles are our practice. Nothing enforces them for you yet. Next: more than one agent.
